sources.//: This `exclude` list is the template engine's own default list MINUS `**/*.lock.json`, and it exists to keep that one pattern off (FS.GG.Templates#384, same root cause as #380). The default is not inert: it strips every `packages.lock.json` out of each generated workspace, so a reviewed lock can never reach a product. Combined with `Directory.Build.props`'s `RestorePackagesWithLockFile=true`, the product's FIRST restore then AUTHORS its own lock from whatever the ambient host happened to resolve, and `RestoreLockedMode=true` enforces that unreviewed lock forever after — surfacing as `NU1403: Package content hash validation failed` the moment the ambient content moves. This template was the most exposed of the four: it committed NO lockfiles at all while still setting `RestoreLockedMode=true` on every project, so every product it generated invented its own lock and called the result locked. Declaring `exclude` here REPLACES the engine default wholesale, so every other default pattern below must be restated verbatim; they are copied from the engine's own defaults, read out of dotnet SDK 10.0.302's Microsoft.TemplateEngine.Orchestrator.RunnableProjects.dll (`strings -el` emits `**/*` as the include, then these six plus `**/*.lock.json` as the exclude). `**/node_modules/**` is restated even though this template ships no npm workspace: the list is the engine default minus exactly one pattern, and a template that silently narrowed a second one would be a difference nobody chose.

productName.description: Raw product name used in paths and assembly metadata. When omitted, --name supplies it.

rootNamespace.description: Optional valid F# identifier supplied by an SDD provider.
